system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Nvidia (NVDA) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Nvidia Acquires Workload Management System Developer SchedMD

BODY:
12:07 PM EST, 12/15/2025 (MT Newswires) -- Nvidia (NVDA) said Monday it has acquired SchedMD, the developer of Slurm, an open-source workload management system for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence.

Financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.

With the acquisition, Nvidia will continue to develop and distribute Slurm as open-source, vendor-neutral software, the company said.

Shares of the company were up 1.6% in recent Monday trading.

Price: 177.83, Change: +2.81, Percent Change: +1.61
</article>

<summary>
[NVDA relevance: primary | sentiment: positive]
Nvidia acquired SchedMD, developer of Slurm, an open-source HPC/AI workload management system. Financial terms undisclosed. Nvidia will continue developing Slurm as open-source, vendor-neutral software. Shares rose 1.6% to 177.83 in Monday trading.
Key facts:
- Nvidia acquired SchedMD, maker of Slurm workload management software
- Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed
- Shares up 1.6% to 177.83 (+2.81) Monday
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article: invented facts,
wrong numbers, wrong direction (e.g. "rose" vs "fell"), wrong company, unattributed rumours stated as fact,
or speculative links to NVDA that the article does not make.
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about NVDA in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a NVDA analyst what matters, and represent how central NVDA really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for NVDA, and says so plainly if NVDA is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the NVDA angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores NVDA, or implies the article is about / important for NVDA when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": ["..."],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
